t.E221.agn: Sulphites are among the substances that must be indicated on the label as allergens in the EU when present at more than 10 mg per kilogram (or litre); they may cause reactions in people with asthma. In its 2022 assessment EFSA withdrew the former temporary daily intake limit (0.7 mg/kg, as SO₂) because data were insufficient, did not set a new limit in its place, and reported a safety concern in high-consuming groups.
t.E221.body: In the stomach and gut, sulphites reach an equilibrium between the sulphite, bisulphite and sulphur dioxide forms; they are largely absorbed from the gut (70–97%). Absorbed sulphite is rapidly converted to sulphate by the enzyme sulphite oxidase, mainly in the liver and small intestine (half-life in humans about 15 minutes); even so, up to a quarter of the amount taken orally may enter the circulation before this conversion.
t.E221.eff.0.a: Labelled above 10 mg per kilogram or litre
t.E221.eff.0.t: May cause respiratory reactions (e.g. worsening of asthma symptoms); in the EU it must be indicated on the label as an allergen
t.E221.eff.0.w: People with asthma and people sensitive to sulphites
t.E221.eff.1.t: EFSA could not establish a safe daily limit and reported a safety concern in high-consuming groups
t.E221.eval: A sulphite-group preservative: in the EU, products containing more than 10 mg/kg (or 10 mg/l) must indicate it on the label as an allergen; it may cause reactions in people with asthma.
t.E221.prod: Produced chemically by reacting sodium hydroxide or sodium carbonate with sulphur dioxide.
t.E221.regx.0: Temporary ADI withdrawn; a safety concern at high consumption has been reported.
t.E221.summary: A preservative and antioxidant that is a sulphur compound. Prevents browning and microbial growth in dried fruit, wine, vinegar and some potato products.
t.E221.what: It is a preservative and antioxidant: it prevents the growth of microorganisms and browning.
